articles.title: Donnie Dunagan, original voice of Disney’s Bambi and triple Purple Heart marine, dies aged 92
articles.summary: Dunagan was six when he voiced the young deer in the classic cartoon, with an assistant director instructing him to pretend his own mother had died. Donnie Dunagan, who voiced Bambi in the Walt Disney classic, as well as playing the son of Frankenstein opposite Basil Rathbone and Boris Karloff, has…
body: Dunagan was six when he was chosen to provide the voice of the young deer in the animation’s most heartbreaking chapter. He recalled the experience in the recording booth as easy and relaxed, with rudimentary technology and notes from an assistant director instructing him to pretend his own mother had died when voicing Bambi’s reaction to his mother being killed by a hunter.
The actor recalled that Bambi’s mother originally dies on screen, but Disney altered this in the edit. Nonetheless, Dunagan received considerable hate mail from the hunting community afterwards.

Bambi, whose release was delayed in the wake of the attack on Pearl Harbor, ended up being Dunagan’s final film. He began his career on horror films Son of Frankenstein and Tower of London, playing the curly blond-haired son of Rathbone’s Dr Frankenstein, as well as featuring in films such as Mother Carey’s Chickens, The Forgotten Woman, Vigil in the Night and Meet the Chump.
He recalled often playing checkers with Karloff on set, while the latter was in full makeup dressed as the monster.

articles.title: Bong Joon Ho on Restoring ‘The Host’ and Why It Still Resonates 20 Years On: ‘We Are Repeating Our Mistakes’
articles.summary: Bong Joon Ho has revisited “The Host” for a 20th-anniversary 4K restoration, and the Oscar-winning director says the 2006 monster movie’s satire of official misinformation feels newly pertinent. Magnolia Pictures will return the remastered film to theaters nationwide on Nov. 20. Screenings on Nov.
body: The ‘Parasite’ director describes how the 4K restoration brings back the film’s original 35mm look, and why its satire of official misinformation lands differently today.
“I can’t believe it’s been 20 years since the release of the film. Time flies,” Bong tells Variety.

In “The Host,” Song Kang-ho plays Gang-du, who nods off on the job at his snack kiosk beside Seoul’s Han River. A monstrous creature crawls out of the water, tears through the crowds on the riverbank and snatches his schoolgirl daughter Hyun-seo, played by Ko A-sung. Authorities declare the creature the carrier of an unknown virus. When Gang-du gets a phone call from Hyun-seo, terrified but alive, he resolves to slip into the sealed-off zone by the river and bring her back. Byun Hee-bong, Park Hae-il and Bae Doo-na co-star as members of his family. New Zealand’s Weta Workshop built detailed models of the creature, and The Orphanage handled visual effects and animation.
Bong’s later film “Parasite” won the Palme d’Or in 2019 and went on to win four Oscars, including best picture, making it the first non-English-language film to take the top prize.

articles.title: Sean Penn, Ava DuVernay and Laura Poitras Turn Out For San Francisco’s Doc Stories
articles.summary: Sean Penn isn’t exactly a fixture on the regional documentary festival circuit. But SFFILM’s Doc Stories has a way of attracting high-profile supporters. On Saturday, Penn was at the fest’s Vogue Theatre in San Francisco to introduce James Marcus Haney’s “Black Sunflowers,” a documentary about a…
body: “Who do you imagine yourself singing like if you could sing like somebody?” Penn told the packed theater. “This movie is the song I dreamed I could sing.”
Penn was one of several Oscar winners at the 12th edition of Doc Stories that concluded on Sunday.

Anne Lai, SFFILM executive director, said the organization’s mission, embodied by Doc Stories and the annual San Francisco Film Festival, is to keep independent voices alive by supporting filmmakers with distinctive work and helping them reach audiences.

“That means not only supporting films and filmmakers who are trying to put distinctive work out into the world, but also growing and sharing that work with audiences,” said Lai. “So as we talk about consolidations of studios and what happens on the margins, I think a lot about us as an organization is trying to look at what is in the margins because a lot of the most interesting things do not come through the mainstream.”

articles.title: Tom Brady and Jim Harbaugh Exec Produce ‘The Team: Michigan Football,’ Set to Debut on Fox This Month (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Fox Sports has greenlighted the two-part documentary “The Team: Michigan Football,” which centers on Michigan’s college football program and its two championship eras. Shadow Lion is behind the series, which is also executive produced by Tom Brady and Jim Harbaugh.
body: Said Brady in a statement: “Thinking about my years at Michigan brings up a lot of emotions because, like many of my teammates, it really shaped who I became as a player and person. I’m excited to share that story alongside the personal experiences of so many others who were transformed by this historic program, and I couldn’t have asked for better partners to do it with than Fox Sports and Shadow Lion.”

Part one, “The Eye of the Storm,” centers on Harbaugh’s relationship to the Michigan football program, including as a player and then leading the team to the 2023 national championship as head coach. Part two, “Those Who Stay,” centers on the team’s 1990s run, including its journey to the 1997 national championship and Brady’s rise as a player.

“It’s been an honor to help tell this story and shed new light on one of the most iconic programs in sports,” said Shadow Lion’s Jeff Fine, director and executive producer, in a statement. “I’m incredibly grateful to the talented team who brought the ‘Those Who Stay Will Be Champions’ mentality to every step of the filmmaking process.”

articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Superfans Hit Theaters for Shane and Ilya on the Big Screen: ‘They Invented Chemistry’
articles.summary: A sea of women and a scattering of men packed into the Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria Sunday night for a cinematic experience. Not to see a new movie, but to celebrate the one-year anniversary of the hit HBO Max-Crave series “Heated Rivalry.” Based on Rachel Reid’s bestselling “Game Changers” books…
body: As fans eagerly await Season 2, which is currently in production, Season 1 was released in theaters, inviting audiences to watch the love story unfold on the big screen for the first time.

Some loyalists donned their best Boston Raiders or Montreal Metros T-shirts, others filled their special edition popcorn buckets and soda cups, but all erupted into raucous cheers while viewing the penultimate and final episodes of the first season. Variety spoke with a few of these “Heated Rivalry” enthusiasts to discuss the appeal of the theater experience and hear what makes the series so special to them.
“I’m down to financially support the show’s success, and also both Hudson and Connor’s success as actors,” Aubrie Shadday, 29, said.

“Seeing it on the big screen with people is so fun, and having the live reaction because everyone watched it essentially by themselves, so hearing everyone giggle or laugh or sniffle here and there is really cool,” Yesenia Vargas, 28, added.

articles.title: 1 in 2 review – compassionate film about dealing with bowel cancer is a personal plea on behalf of the young
articles.summary: David Wilkinson made this warm, generous documentary of his own treatment, and asks why so many much younger people are getting the same diagnosis. ‘I am lucky, as I have become old.” That is the pithy, personal summary offered by English film-maker David Wilkinson, whose previous movie was his…
body: In fact, 1 in 2 is specifically about his shock and sadness that so many people alongside him in waiting rooms, or online in bowel cancer discussion groups are so young, in their 40s, or 30s, or 20s. Wilkinson makes it his business to give these people a voice, along with the medical professionals in the NHS who are battling to help them. He also wants to find something out: why is something that was once considered an old person’s disease on the rise in younger age groups in developed nations? It appears to be due to diet and lifestyle. Could it be microplastics? There are no clearcut answers.

This is a sobering but very compassionate, humorous, generous film, and one that shows how Wilkinson’s highly personal and unselfconsciously confessional style has grown into something very watchable and distinctive. He is the star of this film, but a more self-effacing star can hardly be imagined. It is not fashionable in documentary cinema for the film-maker’s voice and viewpoint to be so explicit, but Wilkinson has gone his own way – without a whole lot of help from the British film establishment – and made a real success of it.

articles.title: ‘We did 10 takes of it!’ Kerr Smith on Dawson’s Creek and filming US TV’s first gay kiss
articles.summary: As he releases a memoir, the actor opens up about the late James Van Der Beek, the magic of the Creek, and facing homophobia for playing gay in the 90s. There are worse things to spend a couple of decades chasing than the feeling of being young, successful and surrounded by people who love you.
body: “I’ve spent the last 25 years of my career trying to re-create that experience,” Smith says of the WB teen drama, on which he played the sensitive jock Jack McPhee for five seasons. “I’ve been trying to measure up to it my entire career.”

Speaking on a Zoom call this October, Smith is now 53, gray-haired and hatted with a brisk demeanor, Smith revisits that pursuit in his new memoir, I Don’t Want to Wait: My Life on Dawson’s Creek. Part oral history and part personal reckoning, the book draws on conversations with former castmates and colleagues, including big-hitters like Katie Holmes, to revisit the series, the protests that followed Jack’s coming-out storyline, and an episode of homophobic harassment Smith had never previously discussed. Highly rhapsodic and wistful about his experience on Dawson’s Creek, Kerr fully embraces the nostalgia in the memoir.

articles.title: ‘Sadistic, forbidden pleasure’: why Gone Girl is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our ongoing series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort films is a reminder of the dark joys that can be found in David Fincher’s devilish thriller.
body: “W hen I think of my wife, I always think of the back of her head,” narrates Ben Affleck in the opening scene of Gone Girl, David Fincher’s 2014 adaptation of the bestselling thriller novel. “I picture cracking her lovely skull, unspooling her brains, trying to get answers to the primal questions of any marriage: What are you thinking? How are you feeling? What have we done to each other?”

From the outset, Gone Girl probably sounds like quite an odd choice for a feelgood movie. The film follows Nick (Affleck) and Amy Dunne (Rosamund Pike), whose once-picture-perfect marriage has become a humiliatingly predictable tale of resentment and infidelity – and when Amy suddenly disappears in suspicious circumstances, it only gets more disturbing. But I find myself being drawn to this film every year when the days start to shorten. There is a strange catharsis (and comfort) in watching a scorned woman get her revenge, one meticulously planned move at a time.

articles.title: Jessica Lange on Bringing ‘Long Day’s Journey Into Night’ Back to the Big Screen, Returning to ‘American Horror Story’ and Retirement Rumors
articles.summary: The legendary stage and screen actress spoke with The Hollywood Reporter at the recent Virginia Film Festival, where she was honored with the fest's Visionary Award.
body: One of only 24 people ever and one of only 10 people still living who have won the “triple crown of acting,” as in, at least one Oscar, Emmy and Tony (she has won two, three and one, respectively), Lange has been a screen actress for 50 years. She made her film debut after being “discovered,” while working part-time as a model, and cast by producer Dino De Laurentiis in his large-scale remake of King Kong (1976). She received a huge publicity build-up, even appearing on the cover of TIME magazine. But the film proved to be such a giant flop that, she explains during this conversation, it shattered her self-confidence and almost destroyed her career.

articles.title: How To Watch Brad Pitt's Heart Of The Beast At Home
articles.summary: Brad Pitt's one-man-and-his-dog survival thriller Heart of the Beast will soon be available to watch at home, along with a few bonus features.
body: David Ayer's "Heart of the Beast" wasn't really a sleeper hit, given that it stars Brad Pitt, but the harrowing survival film turned out to be a surprisingly leggy box office performer thanks to solid word of mouth. Now it's about to find a wider audience as it moves to streaming on November 10 (as the opening of Pitt's kinda-sorta anticipated "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" nears).
Again, "Heart of the Beast" will begin streaming via Premium VOD on November 10, and consumers will get a few extras to go along with their purchase.
